---
title: "Global Pol II footprint-positive LCL clustering"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true
params:
  output: null
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
cfg <- yaml::read_yaml(file.path(params$output, "run_config.yaml"))
here <- file.path(cfg$project, "code/pausing/clustering_Pol2")
source(file.path(here, "pol2_chip_cluster_utils", "pol2_clustering_functions.R"))
source(file.path(here, "pol2_chip_cluster_utils", "pol2_molecule_tables.R"))
source(file.path(here, "pol2_chip_cluster_utils", "pol2_clustering_plots.R"))
pol2_load_helpers(cfg$project)
x <- readRDS(file.path(params$output, "tables", "clustering.rds"))
annotation <- readRDS(file.path(params$output, "tables", "annotations.rds"))
annotation <- pol2_numeric_annotation(annotation)
m <- annotation$molecules
fp <- annotation$footprints
res <- pol2_heatmap_result(x, annotation, cfg$heatmap_max_reads, cfg$seed)
sample_colors <- pol2_sample_colors(cfg, res$assignments$sample_name)
clusters <- levels(res$assignments$cluster)
k <- length(clusters)
```

This is one global clustering across all configured LCL samples. Each included molecule
fully spans the window (−1000 to +999 bp) of a FANTOM5 dominant TSS that lies in a Pol II
IDR peak, and carries at least one 30–60 bp FiberHMM v2 footprint, from its own sample's
`recalled_tf` calls, overlapping that window.
Duplicate footprint records are counted once. Other molecules do not enter clustering.
Denominators use observed m6A sites across all full-window
molecules at each TSS, before random sampling.

The analysis contains `r nrow(m)` randomly selected molecules, out of
`r x$eligible_molecules` eligible ones, from `r uniqueN(m$sample_name)` contributing
samples and `r uniqueN(m$tss_id)` TSSs.
Up to 5,000 unique sample/read molecules are drawn without replacement from all samples
combined, using seed 1. When a molecule qualifies at multiple TSSs, one eligible TSS
is randomly selected for that molecule. Cluster fractions describe this random sample
of the selected population, not all TSS-spanning molecules or cells.
The footprint criterion is candidate evidence for Pol II association, not protein identification.

Clusters are shown in numeric order. Only the Pol II clusters and enrichment
composite retains the saved median pausing-index order, lowest first.

```{r heatmap, fig.width=14, fig.height=11 + 0.55 * k}
pol2_draw_heatmap(pol2_molecule_heatmap(res, sample_colors), clusters, profiles = TRUE)
```

Heatmap, average profiles with the median PI, and bulk Pol II ChIP fold-enrichment over
each molecule's TSS region (−50 to +299 bp; log2 of the cluster mean over the mean of all
molecules, Wilcoxon test of the cluster against all others, BH over clusters), in the
layout of Fig. 1c of the nano-NOMe-seq paper.

```{r pol2-clusters-and-enrichment, fig.width=16, fig.height=max(7, 0.9 * k + 2)}
pol2_clusters_and_enrichment(res, annotation, sample_colors)
```

```{r summary}
knitr::kable(annotation$summary, digits = 3)
```

```{r footprints, fig.width=10, fig.height=1.4 * k + 2.5}
pol2_plot_footprints(annotation)
```

Each molecule's footprints, one row per molecule in the heatmap's order. Nucleosomes
(130–160 bp) are fibertools nucleosome calls; TF footprints (10–30, 30–60, 60–80 bp) are
FiberHMM v2 `recalled_tf` blocks of the molecule's own sample (`tracks` stage).

```{r footprint-molecules, fig.width=9, fig.height=11 + 0.55 * k}
pol2_plot_footprint_molecules(res, fread(file.path(params$output, "tables", "tracks", "molecule_footprints.tsv.gz")))
```

Pol II fold-enrichment is measured over each candidate footprint. The boxplot
summarizes a molecule's footprints first, to avoid giving molecules with several
footprints extra weight. Bulk Pol II signal is shared locus evidence, not an independent
measurement of polymerase binding on each molecule.

```{r signal, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
signal <- fp[, .(signal = if (all(is.na(pol2_mean))) NA_real_ else mean(pol2_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(cluster, observation_id)]
ggplot(signal, aes(cluster, signal)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Mean Pol II fold-enrichment across candidate footprints")
```

PI is joined by Ensembl gene ID; the RefSeq TSS of `pause_index.tsv` can differ from the
FANTOM5 TSS used here.

```{r pi, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
pi_sites <- unique(m[, .(cluster, tss_id, pi)])
if (any(is.finite(pi_sites$pi))) {
  print(ggplot(pi_sites[is.finite(pi)], aes(cluster, pi)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
          scale_y_log10() + theme_bw() + labs(y = "PI (one value per TSS within each cluster)"))
} else cat("No matching PI values have been supplied.")
```

## Example loci

All eligible molecules at the FANTOM5 TSS of each gene in `locus_genes` (config), drawn
with `plot_locus_molecules()` from `parsing_functions/plotting_functions.r`. It is the
HSCA domain/CTCF figure without its CTCF, loop and domain tracks. Clustered molecules
keep their Leiden cluster. Every other molecule at the TSS takes the majority cluster of
its 10 nearest clustered molecules (Manhattan distance on the 40 bin features). The bars
compare the cluster proportions at the TSS with those of all clustered molecules.
Diamonds mark the gene's GTEx v8 LCL eVariants in the window.

```{r loci, include=FALSE}
loci <- pol2_locus_figures(cfg, x, annotation)
```

```{r loci-figures, fig.width=12, fig.height=if (length(loci)) max(vapply(loci, function(l) l$height, numeric(1))) else 1}
for (gene in names(loci)) print(loci[[gene]]$combined)
```

## Imprinted loci

Counts use all projected eligible physical molecules, deduplicated by RID within
cluster. Molecules seen at both imprinted and other TSSs appear only in the
imprinted composition bar. These comparisons are descriptive; no test is applied.

```{r imprinting, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.5}
imprinting <- pol2_imprinting(cfg,
  fread(file.path(params$output,"tables","tracks","molecule_projection.tsv.gz")),
  pol2_read_prepared(cfg)$tss, clusters)
pol2_plot_imprinting(imprinting, clusters)
knitr::kable(imprinting$loci, digits = 3)
```

## Features of the 5,000 clustered molecules

m6A uses the stored calls and observed-site denominators from all full-span reads
at each TSS; its pooled fraction is sum(calls) / sum(positions). CpG uses
pb-CpG-tools count mode on these molecules, restricted to their cluster's TSS
windows. CpG boxplots assign each molecule its cluster/TSS fraction; the pooled
fraction counts each genomic CpG once per cluster. GRO-cap is the sense-strand
read sum over the full 2 kb window; DNase is the mean over that window.
Diamonds show pooled methylation fractions or molecule-weighted mean signal.
GRO-cap and DNase are plotted as log10(x + 1). Saved result tables permit
re-plotting without extracting CpG again.

```{r cluster-features, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
features <- list(
  molecules = fread(file.path(params$output, "tables", "cluster_features", "cluster_feature_molecules.tsv.gz")),
  summary = fread(file.path(params$output, "tables", "cluster_features", "cluster_features.tsv")))
pol2_plot_cluster_features(features, clusters)
knitr::kable(features$summary, digits = 3)
```

## Per-molecule promoter autocorrelation

Binary m6A accessibility calls are analyzed separately in two strand-relative
windows for each saved clustered molecule: upstream −500..−25 bp and downstream
+25..+500 bp (inclusive; 476 bases each). The windows are never concatenated.
Each window uses its own mean and variance; a molecule can be excluded in one
window and retained in the other. These are not
inferred nucleosome occupancy or the 40-bin clustering features. Fully covered
bases without calls are zero. Each curve is mean-centered and divided by
sum((x − mean(x))²), with no lag-dependent overlap correction. Cluster curves
are equal-weight means of valid molecule ACFs. Zero-variance molecules have
undefined ACFs and retain the original function’s zero-variance status.

All lags 0..475 bp are saved for each window; curves and heatmaps focus on 15..475 bp. Large lags
have fewer overlapping bases and the fixed normalization attenuates them.
Counts and uncertainty estimates are omitted as requested; no resampling is
performed, so there is no resampling unit. Peaks are descriptive strongest
positive local maxima in 140..250 bp, using the existing peak finder, and do
not establish nucleosome spacing. Cluster-mean peaks are not averages of
individual molecule peak positions.

```{r autocorrelation-analysis, include=FALSE}
acf_plots <- local({
# Configuration/I/O only. All ACF computation, summaries and plots use originals.
# Source with cfg and optionally acf_action="plot" to load plots without computing.
tables <- file.path(cfg$output, "tables")
acf_tables <- file.path(tables,"autocorrelation")
dir.create(acf_tables,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
acf_action <- if (isTRUE(get0("recompute_autocorrelation",ifnotfound=FALSE)) || !file.exists(file.path(acf_tables,"autocorrelation_cluster_summary.tsv.gz"))) "compute" else "plot"
if (acf_action == "compute") {
  x <- readRDS(file.path(tables,"clustering.rds"))
  m <- data.table::fread(file.path(tables,"molecule_assignments.tsv.gz"))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(m$observation_id),nrow(m)==nrow(x$molecules))
  index <- match(m$observation_id,x$molecules$observation_id)
  for (field in c("sample_name","original_RID","tss_id","cluster"))
    stopifnot(identical(as.character(m[[field]]),as.character(x$molecules[[field]][index])))
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(x$sites),as.character(-1000:999)))
  sites <- as.matrix(x$sites[match(m$observation_id,rownames(x$sites)),,drop=FALSE])
  tmp <- tempfile("pol2_acf_"); dir.create(tmp)
  writeBin(as.raw(t(sites)),file.path(tmp,"calls.bin"))
  data.table::fwrite(m,file.path(tmp,"metadata.tsv"),sep="\t")
  worker <- file.path(tmp,"call_original_acf.py")
  writeLines(r"---("""I/O adapter: call the original ACF, peak and cluster-summary functions."""
from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

shared = Path(sys.argv[4]) / 'code/clustering_methods/auto_correlation'
acf = runpy.run_path(str(shared / '03_compute_autocorrelations.py'))['autocorrelations']
summary_functions = runpy.run_path(str(shared / '05_summarize_autocorrelations.py'))
metadata = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[2], sep='\t')
binary = np.fromfile(sys.argv[1], dtype=np.uint8).reshape(len(metadata), 2000)
output = Path(sys.argv[3])
windows = {'upstream': (-500, -25), 'downstream': (25, 500)}
curves, stats, molecule_tables = [], [], []
for window, bounds in windows.items():
    profiles, valid = acf(binary, positions=np.arange(-1000, 1000), window=bounds)
    selected = binary[:, bounds[0]+1000:bounds[1]+1001]
    records = metadata.copy()
    records['cluster'] = records.cluster.str.replace('cluster', '', regex=False).astype(int)
    records['status'] = np.where(valid, 'clustered', 'zero_variance')
    records['region_id'] = window
    records['m6a_call_fraction'] = selected.mean(axis=1)
    averages, summaries, _ = summary_functions['summarize'](profiles, records)
    for table in [averages, summaries]:
        table['cluster'] = 'cluster' + table.cluster.astype(str)
        table['window'] = window
        table['window_start_bp'], table['window_end_bp'] = bounds
    curves.append(averages[['cluster','window','window_start_bp','window_end_bp','lag_bp','mean_acf']])
    stats.append(summaries[['cluster','window','window_start_bp','window_end_bp',
                           'positive_local_peak_140_250_bp','peak_acf']])
    records['cluster'] = metadata.cluster
    records['window'] = window
    records['window_start_bp'], records['window_end_bp'] = bounds
    peaks = [summary_functions['repeat_peak'](profile) for profile in profiles]
    records['positive_local_peak_140_250_bp'] = [p[0] for p in peaks]
    records['peak_acf'] = [p[1] for p in peaks]
    molecule_tables.append(records)
    np.savez_compressed(output / f'autocorrelation_per_molecule_{window}.npz', acf=profiles,
                        lag_bp=np.arange(selected.shape[1]), relative_bp=np.arange(bounds[0],bounds[1]+1),
                        observation_id=metadata.observation_id.to_numpy(dtype=str), window=np.array(window))
pd.concat(curves).to_csv(output/'autocorrelation_cluster_summary.tsv.gz',sep='\t',index=False)
pd.concat(stats).to_csv(output/'autocorrelation_cluster_peaks.tsv',sep='\t',index=False)
pd.concat(molecule_tables).to_csv(output/'autocorrelation_molecules.tsv.gz',sep='\t',index=False)
)---",worker)
  status <- system2(cfg$python,shQuote(c("-B",worker,file.path(tmp,"calls.bin"),file.path(tmp,"metadata.tsv"),acf_tables,cfg$project)))
  unlink(tmp,recursive=TRUE)
  if (status != 0L) stop("Autocorrelation worker failed")
  saveRDS(list(window=list(upstream=c(-500,-25),downstream=c(25,500)),lags=c(0,475),
    method="Original autocorrelations(), summarize(), repeat_peak(); binary 1-bp m6A",
    input_md5=tools::md5sum(file.path(tables,c("clustering.rds","molecule_assignments.tsv.gz")))),
    file.path(acf_tables,"autocorrelation_provenance.rds"))
}
pol2_autocorrelation_plots(cfg, save = acf_action == "compute")
})
```

```{r autocorrelation-overlay, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
for (window in c("upstream", "downstream")) print(acf_plots[[paste0(window,"_overlay")]])
```

```{r autocorrelation-panels, fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
for (window in c("upstream", "downstream")) print(acf_plots[[paste0(window,"_panels")]])
knitr::kable(fread(file.path(params$output, "tables", "autocorrelation", "autocorrelation_cluster_peaks.tsv")), digits = 4)
```

```{r autocorrelation-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
for (window in c("upstream", "downstream")) print(acf_plots[[paste0(window,"_heatmap")]])
```

The heatmap shows the same cluster-mean autocorrelation values as the curves,
with clusters 1 through 7 from top to bottom.

## Nucleosome positioning using the original functions

The original `process_nuc_pos.R` and `plot_nuc_pos.R` functions are used directly.
FiberHMM BED13 nucleosome blocks come from each molecule's own LCL sample,
without a size filter. FANTOM5 TSS anchors and the strand-oriented −1000..+999 bp
window are the saved clustering inputs. Full footprint boundaries determine
inferred centers; these are not directly measured histone dyads.

Occupancy is evaluated at grid positions 10 bp apart, with spanning molecules
as denominators and each molecule counted once per position. Profiles pool
molecules within each cluster. Raw inferred-center counts use 25-bp bins. Successful
input extraction with no returned calls follows the original zero-call convention.
No separate missing-data analysis is performed; input-read failures stop the run.

−1/+1 use the original **midpoint** definition: the closest negative center and
closest nonnegative center, respectively. A TSS-covering footprint may therefore
be assigned to one side. Missing flanks remain NA and are not evidence of loss.
No gap is computed. TSS occupancy is also reported separately, with 95% intervals
from 500 crossed promoter × biological-sample bootstrap draws, not independent
molecule resampling. These patterns are conditional on the existing Pol II
footprint-positive accessibility clusters and are not independent validation.

```{r nucleosome-analysis, include=FALSE}
nuc_plots <- if (isTRUE(get0("recompute_nucleosome",ifnotfound=FALSE)) ||
    !file.exists(file.path(cfg$output,"tables","nuc","nucleosome_cluster_summary.tsv.gz"))) local({
# Configuration, joins and output routing only: source and call original functions.
source(file.path(cfg$project,"code/nucleosome_positioning/process_nuc_pos.R"),local=TRUE)
tables <- file.path(cfg$output,"tables")
nuc_tables <- file.path(tables,"nuc")
dir.create(nuc_tables,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
prep <- readRDS(file.path(tables,"prepared.rds"))
x <- readRDS(file.path(tables,"clustering.rds"))
m <- fread(file.path(tables,"molecule_assignments.tsv.gz"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(m$observation_id),nrow(m)==nrow(x$molecules))
idx <- match(m$observation_id,x$molecules$observation_id)
for (field in c("sample_name","original_RID","tss_id","cluster","tss","strand"))
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(m[[field]]),as.character(x$molecules[[field]][idx])))
clusters <- pol2_numeric_clusters(m$cluster)
m[, cluster:=factor(cluster,levels=clusters)]
site <- prep$tss[match(unique(m$tss_id),tss_id)]
anchors <- build_region_anchors(NULL,NULL,NULL,relative_window=c(-1000L,999L),
  anchor_table=site[,.(region_id=tss_id,chr=chrom,anchor=tss,strand,region_type="promoter",gene=gene_name,ensg=gene_id)])
stopifnot(all(anchors$view_start==site$window_start+1L),all(anchors$view_end==site$window_end))
reads <- build_read_table(m[,.(region_id=tss_id,RID=observation_id,sample_name,original_RID,
  biological_sample=cell_line,cluster,read_start,read_end)],anchors)
reads[,`:=`(rel_read_start=pmax(rel_read_start,-1000L),rel_read_end=pmin(rel_read_end,999L))]
stopifnot(all(reads$rel_read_start == -1000L),all(reads$rel_read_end == 999L))
paths <- setNames(file.path(cfg$footprint_dir,prep$samples$sample_name,
  paste0(prep$samples$sample_name,".recalled_footprint.bed.gz")),prep$samples$sample_name)
footprints <- extract_region_footprints(reads,anchors,input_paths=paths,include_tf=FALSE,original_id_col="original_RID")
footprints <- merge(footprints,reads[,.(region_id,RID,sample_name,original_RID,biological_sample,cluster)],
  by=c("region_id","RID","sample_name"))
pos <- read_position_summary(footprints,reads,include_gap=FALSE)
strata <- position_summary_by_group(pos,by=c("region_id","cluster","sample_name"),include_gap=FALSE)
summary <- position_summary_by_group(pos,by="cluster",include_gap=FALSE,bootstrap=500L,sample_col="biological_sample")
occupancy <- occupancy_profile(footprints,reads,anchors,by=c("region_id","cluster","sample_name"))
centers <- occupancy_profile(footprints,reads,anchors,by=c("region_id","cluster","sample_name"),bin_size=25L,metric="centers")
# Pool the original molecule counts within each cluster.
occ_profile <- occupancy[,.(value=sum(n_occupied)/sum(n_reads),
  raw_count=sum(n_occupied),denominator=sum(n_reads)),by=.(cluster,pos)]
center_profile <- centers[,.(value=sum(n_centers),raw_count=sum(n_centers)),
  by=.(cluster,pos,bin_start,bin_end_exclusive,bin_width_bp)]
objects <- list(molecules=pos,footprints=footprints,occupancy_profiles=occ_profile,center_counts_profiles=center_profile,
  cluster_summary=summary,positional_strata=strata,occupancy_strata=occupancy,center_counts_strata=centers[,!"density"],
  centers=footprints[,.(region_id,RID,sample_name,original_RID,biological_sample,cluster,fp_start,fp_end,rel_mid)])
for (name in names(objects)) fwrite(objects[[name]],file.path(nuc_tables,paste0("nucleosome_",name,".tsv.gz")),sep="\t")
nuc_plots <- pol2_nucleosome_plots(cfg, save = TRUE)
saveRDS(list(window=c(-1000L,999L),input_paths=paths,source="FiberHMM recalled_footprint BED13; all blocks; no size filter",
  selection="Existing Pol II footprint-positive accessibility clusters",position_method="Original midpoint-based -1/+1; no gap",
  uncertainty="TSS occupancy: 500 crossed promoter x biological-sample bootstrap draws; no molecule resampling",
  inputs=tools::md5sum(file.path(tables,c("clustering.rds","prepared.rds","molecule_assignments.tsv.gz")))),
  file.path(nuc_tables,"nucleosome_provenance.rds"))
nuc_plots
}) else pol2_nucleosome_plots(cfg)
```

```{r nucleosome-profiles, fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
print(nuc_plots$center_counts)
```



## Expression and pausing index

Expression is mean ENCSR820PHH gene TPM across the two configured replicates,
joined by version-stripped Ensembl gene ID. Each TSS is represented once per
cluster; the summaries are descriptive and TSSs shared between clusters are not
independent biological replicates.

```{r expression-analysis, include=FALSE}
expression_result <- local({
tables <- file.path(cfg$output, "tables")

expr <- rbindlist(lapply(cfg$expression, function(f) fread(f, select = c("gene_id", "TPM"))))
expr <- expr[grepl("^ENSG", gene_id) & !grepl("_PAR_Y$", gene_id),
             .(tpm = mean(TPM), n_rep = .N), by = .(gene_key = sub("\\..*$", "", gene_id))]
stopifnot(all(expr$n_rep == length(cfg$expression)))

summary <- fread(file.path(tables, "cluster_summary.tsv"))
m <- fread(file.path(tables, "molecule_assignments.tsv.gz"))
tss <- unique(m[, .(cluster, tss_id, gene_id, gene_name, pi)])
tss[, tpm := expr$tpm[match(sub("\\..*$", "", gene_id), expr$gene_key)]]
tss[, cluster := factor(cluster, levels = pol2_numeric_clusters(summary$cluster))]
message(sum(is.na(tss$tpm)), " of ", nrow(tss), " cluster/TSS pairs have no TPM")

d <- tss[is.finite(tpm)]
out <- d[, {
  ok <- is.finite(pi) & is.finite(tpm)
  correlation <- if(sum(ok)>=3L) suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(pi[ok],tpm[ok],method="spearman")) else NULL
  list(n_tss=.N,median_tpm=median(tpm),frac_tpm_ge1=mean(tpm>=1),median_pi=median(pi,na.rm=TRUE),
    rho_pi_tpm=if(is.null(correlation)) NA_real_ else unname(correlation$estimate),
    p_rho=if(is.null(correlation)) NA_real_ else correlation$p.value,n_pi_tpm=sum(ok))
},by=cluster]
# TPM of each cluster's TSSs against all other clusters' TSSs.
out[, p_tpm_vs_rest := vapply(as.character(cluster), function(cl)
  stats::wilcox.test(d[cluster == cl, tpm], d[cluster != cl, tpm])$p.value, numeric(1))]
out[, `:=`(fdr_rho = adjust_bh(p_rho), fdr_tpm_vs_rest = adjust_bh(p_tpm_vs_rest))]
setorder(out, cluster)
kw <- stats::kruskal.test(tpm ~ cluster, data = d)
print(out)

colors <- cluster_id_palette(levels(d$cluster))
boxes <- ggplot(d, aes(cluster, log10(tpm + 1), fill = cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Cluster (numeric order)", y = "log10(TPM + 1)", title = "Expression of each cluster's TSSs",
       subtitle = sprintf("ENCSR820PHH, mean of 2 replicates; Kruskal-Wallis p = %.2g", kw$p.value)) +
  theme_fiberseq("classic", base_size = 10)
labels <- out[, .(cluster, label = sprintf("rho = %.2f\nn = %d", rho_pi_tpm, n_pi_tpm))]
scatter <- ggplot(d[is.finite(pi) & pi > 0], aes(log10(pi), log10(tpm + 1), colour = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) + facet_wrap(~cluster, nrow = 1) +
  geom_text(data = labels, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "log10(pausing index)", y = "log10(TPM + 1)", title = "Pausing index vs expression within each cluster (Spearman)") +
  theme_fiberseq("bw", base_size = 10)
combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(boxes, scatter, ncol=1,rel_heights=c(1,.9))
save_figure(combined,file.path(cfg$output,"plots","pi_expression_by_cluster.pdf"),width=14,height=8)
list(plot=combined,summary=out)
})
```

```{r expression-figure, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
knitr::kable(expression_result$summary,digits=3)
```

## Histone marks at the TSS

Bulk GM12878 histone ChIP-seq fold change over control (`histone_marks` in config:
ENCODE4 GRCh38 reprocessing of the Broad ENCODE2 experiments, pooled replicates) around
each clustered molecule's FANTOM5 TSS, strand-oriented. Each 50-bp bin is the
coverage-weighted mean signal. A cluster's curve is the mean over its molecules, so a
TSS weighs in proportion to its molecules. Each panel shows one histone mark, with
all cluster curves overlaid in numeric order and no all-molecule reference. The ChIP is GM12878 locus-level evidence, not a measurement on each molecule
or donor, and molecules at the same TSS share its signal. Descriptive only.

```{r histone-analysis, include=FALSE}
histone_result <- local({
  profiles <- pol2_histone_profiles(cfg, fread(file.path(cfg$output, "tables", "molecule_assignments.tsv.gz")))
  fwrite(profiles, file.path(cfg$output, "tables", "histone_cluster_profiles.tsv.gz"), sep = "\t")
  plot <- pol2_plot_histone_profiles(profiles, clusters)
  save_figure(plot, file.path(cfg$output, "plots", "histone_profiles_by_cluster.pdf"), width = 16, height = 4.5)
  stacked <- pol2_plot_histone_profiles(profiles, clusters, stacked = TRUE)
  save_figure(stacked, file.path(cfg$output, "plots", "histone_profiles_by_cluster_stacked.pdf"), width = 16, height = 12)
  list(overlay = plot, stacked = stacked)
})
```

```{r histone-figure, fig.width=16, fig.height=4.5}
print(histone_result$overlay)
```


The second view stacks clusters 1–7 vertically, with one histone mark per column.
Each mark uses the same y-axis range across clusters; the all-molecule reference
is omitted.

```{r histone-stacked-figure, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
print(histone_result$stacked)
```
